header.name: Speech and Audio Processing
header.description: This is an introductory course on Speech and Audio pocessing offered to undergraduate and graduate students. The goal is to develop understanding of a wide range of important concepts that comprise the field of digital speech/audio processing and enable students to develop practical applications.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate a systematic understanding of the main concepts in speech and audio processing.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to describe and explain the principles of pattern recognition in relation to speech processing including feature extraction, hidden Markov modelling and psychoacoustics.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply the concepts and methods learned to some speech processing problems, such as, pitch estimation, speech recognition/synthesis and speech coding.

lecture_topics: Introduction - Speech and language. Speech processing applications.
Characteristics of speech signals and review of related DSP fundamentals.
Speech Production - Vocal tract description. Source-filter model
All-pole digital model of vocal tract. Pitch, formants and anti-resonance.
Speech Perception - The structure of the ear.
Frequency and amplitude response of ear. Perception units.
Signal Processing Techniques I - Autocorrelation, Pitch estimation,. Fourier analysis, Spectrogram
Signal Processing Techniques II - Spectral analysis of voiced/unvoiced speech, formants and antiresonances. Harmonic signal processing..
Linear Prediction I - Z-transform, vocal tract transfer function, linear prediction model, all-pole source filter.
Linear Prediction II - LPC coefficients estimation. Speech synthesis from the LPC coefficients.
Inverse Filtering of Speech Signal - Separating source from excitation
Sparse LP modelling - L1 vs L2 regularized solutions
Cepstral Analysis
Cepstral Deconvolution
Overflow/Break
Overflow/Break
Psychoacoustics I - Loudness perception, pitch perception
Psychoacoustics II - auditory masking, timbre perception, spatial hearing
Introduction to Speech Coding
Introduction to Audio Coding
Template matching - Dynamic time warping
GMM and Hidden Markov model
Discussion: Group delay functions for speech processing
Discussion: Phase modelling of speech signals
Catch-up and revision
